newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire envoy says Mandela promises big peace role.
newsitem.headline: Zaire envoy says Mandela promises big peace role.

text.p: A senior Zairean envoy said on Thursday South African President Nelson Mandela had promised a big role in peace efforts in troubled Central Africa.
It was not immediately clear what Mandela's role would be in attempts to end fighting in the Great Lakes region where the Zairean army has battled ethnic Tutsi rebels supported by Rwanda.

"(Zairean) President Mobutu has asked his colleague (Mandela) to play a major diplomatic role in this conflict...and he is going to play the role that is expected from him in the situation that is occurring in Zaire," special envoy Honore Ngbanda told a news conference a day after talks with Mandela.
Ngbanda, special security adviser to Mobutu, did not say what role Mandela would take but said the South African government had also promised to provide humanitarian assistance in eastern Zaire.
Former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere, a senior African statesman, is expected in South Africa on Saturday to discuss the country's role in regional peace efforts.

South Africa announced on Wednesday it had suspended arms sales to Rwanda and indicated it would contribute troops to an international force for Zaire if asked to do so by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.

East and Central African leaders decided earlier this week to push for a neutral force to oversee safe corridors to allow humanitarian aid to reach over a million refugees, mainly Rwandan Hutus, in eastern Zaire.
Prospects for an intervention force were boosted after an all-clear from ailing Mobutu, who said in France he backed an initiative on intervention.
Tutsi rebels who have overwhelmed the Zaire army in two eastern provinces oppose the deployment of a foreign force.
